summary.text: A 79-year-old man with no significant past medical history presented after multiple falls, having been found on the floor by a neighbor for an estimated nine hours. He was diffusely jaundiced, icteric, confused and poorly kept, with severe acute kidney injury, hyperbilirubinemia and severe thrombocytopenia on initial laboratory testing; he lived alone.

Abdominal ultrasound was concerning for acalculous cholecystitis, a HIDA scan showed no visualization of the gallbladder, and MRCP was consistent with acute cholecystitis without cirrhosis. Infectious panels for EBV, CMV, HIV and hepatitis were negative, and alcohol abuse was ruled out by the MRCP findings and a negative phosphatidylethanol. He received fluids, intravenous Zosyn, lactulose, rifaximin, albumin and Protonix, plus thiamine, folate and vitamin B12 for severe deficiency.

During admission he developed bilateral deep venous thrombosis and a V/Q scan concerning for pulmonary embolism, and an IVC filter was placed because heparin was contraindicated. Over three days BUN, creatinine and bilirubin rose and platelets fell; hematology gave IVIG twice. Hepatology and general surgery recommended a cholecystostomy drain, which IR judged unnecessary.

Questioning of his daughter revealed an unhygienic home with three dogs and two chickens. On day five of admission labs began to improve, Leptospira IgM antibody titers were positive, and leptospirosis was diagnosed. Discharge labs showed BUN 26 mg/dL, creatinine 1.29 mg/dL, total bilirubin 8.2 mg/dL and platelets 239 x10^(3)/µL, and infectious disease cleared him for discharge after adequate antibiotic coverage.
